claim: Non-linear summation of synaptic inputs to the dendrites of pyramidal neurons has been proposed to increase the computation capacity of neurons through coincidence detection, signal amplification, and additional logic operations such as XOR.

evidence: This claim references prior research findings.

claim: Supralinear dendritic integration of near-synchronous spatially clustered glutamate-receptor mediated depolarization occurs in NDNF-positive neurogliaform cells in the mouse hippocampus.
source: Here, we use patch-clamp electrophysiology, and two-photon calcium imaging and glutamate uncaging, to show that supralinear dendritic integration of near-synchronous spatially clustered glutamate-receptor mediated depolarization occurs in NDNF-positive neurogliaform cells and oriens-lacunosum moleculare interneurons in the mouse hippocampus.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon imaging.

claim: Supralinear dendritic integration of near-synchronous spatially clustered glutamate-receptor mediated depolarization occurs in oriens-lacunosum moleculare interneurons in the mouse hippocampus.

claim: Supralinear summation in neurogliaform cells was detected via recordings of somatic depolarizations elicited by uncaging of glutamate on dendritic fragments.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of somatic voltage responses.

claim: Supralinearity in neurogliaform cells was abolished by blocking NMDA receptors.

claim: Supralinearity in neurogliaform cells resisted blockade of voltage-gated sodium channels.

claim: Blocking L-type calcium channels abolished supralinear calcium signalling in neurogliaform cells.

claim: NMDAR-dependent supralinear EPSP summation in PV+ basket cells was only seen in dendrites receiving feedback excitation in stratum oriens and not in dendrites receiving feed-forward excitation in stratum radiatum.
source: Using multiphoton glutamate uncaging for increased spatial precision, Cornford et al., 2019 also showed evidence for NMDAR-dependent supralinear EPSP summation in PV+ basket cells, although this was only seen in dendrites receiving feedback excitation in stratum oriens and not in dendrites receiving feed-forward excitation in stratum radiatum.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Somatic action potentials attenuate rapidly as they back-propagate in PV+ dendrites.
source: Failure to detect supralinear summation in stratum radiatum dendrites of PV+ interneurons is consistent with evidence from dendritic recordings that somatic action potentials attenuate rapidly as they back-propagate, and that PV+ dendrites express abundant Kv3 family potassium channels and relatively few sodium channels (Hu and Vervaeke, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: PV+ dendrites express abundant Kv3 family potassium channels and relatively few sodium channels.

claim: Neurogliaform cells support feed-forward inhibition.
source: We therefore set out to characterize dendritic integration in two types of interneurons innervating the distal dendrites of CA1 pyramidal neurons: PV-negative neurogliaform interneurons, which support feed-forward inhibition, and oriens-lacunosum moleculare (OLM) cells, which additionally mediate feedback inhibition.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about neurogliaform cells.

claim: OLM cells mediate feedback inhibition.
source: We therefore set out to characterize dendritic integration in two types of interneurons innervating the distal dendrites of CA1 pyramidal neurons: PV-negative neurogliaform interneurons, which support feed-forward inhibition, and oriens-lacunosum moleculare (OLM) cells, which additionally mediate feedback inhibition.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about OLM cells.

claim: Neurogliaform cells and OLM cells innervate the distal dendrites of CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: We therefore set out to characterize dendritic integration in two types of interneurons innervating the distal dendrites of CA1 pyramidal neurons: PV-negative neurogliaform interneurons, which support feed-forward inhibition, and oriens-lacunosum moleculare (OLM) cells, which additionally mediate feedback inhibition.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about these interneuron types.

claim: The axons of neurogliaform cells and OLM cells innervate the apical tuft dendrites of pyramidal neurons in the SLM.
source: Although their cell bodies reside in different layers, and their developmental origin and intrinsic properties are strikingly different (Pelkey et al., 2017; Asgarian et al., 2019; Booker and Wyllie, 2021; Sik et al., 1995; Chittajallu et al., 2017; Price et al., 2005; Tricoire et al., 2010), their axons innervate the same targets, the apical tuft dendrites of pyramidal neurons in the SLM.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Neurogliaform cells receive inputs from the entorhinal cortex and the nucleus reuniens.
source: Neurogliaform cells receive inputs from the entorhinal cortex and the nucleus reuniens (Chittajallu et al., 2017), with distinct plasticity rules at synapses made by these afferents (Mercier et al., 2022), and a subset can be identified in stratum lacunosum-moleculare (SLM) using knock-in mice expressing cre recombinase at the neuron-derived neurotrophic factor (Ndnf) locus (Chittajallu et al., 2017; Tricoire et al., 2010; Mercier et al., 2022; Booker and Vida, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

source: OLM cells, in contrast, have their cell bodies and dendrites in stratum oriens, are excited by axon collaterals of both CA1 and CA3 pyramidal neurons, and can be identified using mice expressing cre at the somatostatin locus (Taniguchi et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge about OLM cells.

claim: OLM cells are excited by axon collaterals of both CA1 and CA3 pyramidal neurons.

claim: In a representative neurogliaform interneuron, the somatic uEPSP evoked by near-synchronous uncaging was substantially greater in amplitude and duration than predicted from the arithmetic sum of the individual somatic uEPSPs.
source: In the illustrated example, the somatic uEPSP evoked by near-synchronous uncaging was substantially greater in amplitude and duration than predicted from the arithmetic sum of the individual somatic uEPSPs (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: In a representative neurogliaform interneuron, the amplitude of the dendritic calcium fluorescence transient increased abruptly with 6 or more near-synchronous uncaging locations.
source: This revealed a discontinuity, where the amplitude of the dendritic calcium fluorescence transient increased abruptly with 6 or more near-synchronous uncaging locations, and exceeded the fluorescence observed with asynchronous uncaging at all 12 locations (Figure 1e and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: In a representative neurogliaform interneuron, the dendritic calcium fluorescence transient with 6 or more near-synchronous uncaging locations exceeded the fluorescence observed with asynchronous uncaging at all 12 locations.
source: This revealed a discontinuity, where the amplitude of the dendritic calcium fluorescence transient increased abruptly with 6 or more near-synchronous uncaging locations, and exceeded the fluorescence observed with asynchronous uncaging at all 12 locations (Figure 1e and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: The overall average amplitude supralinearity in neurogliaform cells was 58 ± 20%.
source: Including cells that were used for subsequent blockade of NMDARs (see below), the overall average amplitude supralinearity was 58 ± 20% (average ± SEM, n=11, deviation from 0, p<0.001; Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 11 cells shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The degree of voltage nonlinearity in neurogliaform cells was more marked for the voltage integral measured over 100ms (integral nonlinearity 122 ± 35%).
source: Consistent with the data from the sample neuron (Figure 1) the degree of voltage nonlinearity was more marked for the voltage integral measured over 100ms (integral nonlinearity 122 ± 35%), implying the involvement of slow and/or regenerating conductances (Figure 2c and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: Six out of seven neurogliaform interneurons where dendritic calcium transients were measured exhibited a greater than predicted Fluo-4 fluorescence transient, with a nonlinearity estimated at 37 ± 10%.
source: As for dendritic calcium transients, six out of seven interneurons where they were measured exhibited a greater than predicted Fluo-4 fluorescence transient, with a nonlinearity estimated at 37 ± 10% (p=0.0138; Figure 2e and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 7 cells shown in Figure 2e and f.

claim: D-AP5 robustly abolished voltage supralinearity in neurogliaform cells, whether measured as the peak amplitude of uEPSPs or uEPSP integral.
source: In a subset of cells reported in Figure 2, we applied the NMDAR antagonist D-AP5 by bath perfusion. This robustly abolished voltage supralinearity, whether measured as the peak amplitude of uEPSPs (p<0.001, n=6; Figure 3a, c and d) or uEPSP integral (p<0.001; Figure 3e and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 6 cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: Summation of somatic uEPSPs in neurogliaform cells became sublinear with NMDARs blocked.
source: Summation of somatic uEPSPs became sublinear (p<0.001, p<0.001, for peak and integral respectively), consistent with the behaviour of a passive dendrite where the local synaptic driving force and impedance diminish as an increasing number of glutamate receptors open.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with D-AP5.

claim: Dendritic calcium fluorescence transients in neurogliaform cells were profoundly reduced by D-AP5.
source: Dendritic calcium fluorescence transients were also profoundly reduced (Figure 3b, g and h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b, g and h.

claim: Robust supralinear integration was seen for both uEPSPs and calcium fluorescence transients in neurogliaform cells in the presence of TTX.
source: We examined the role of voltage-gated sodium channels, which have been implicated in back-propagating action potentials in principal cells (Buzsáki and Kandel, 1998; Stuart and Sakmann, 1994; Stuart et al., 1997), by repeating the study in the continuous presence of tetrodotoxin (TTX). In a representative cell, robust supralinear integration was seen for both uEPSPs (Figure 4a) and calcium fluorescence transients (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: Across all dendrites tested in TTX (n=7), both the uEPSP and the dendritic calcium transient amplitudes summated supralinearity in neurogliaform cells.
source: Across all dendrites tested (n=7), both the uEPSP and the dendritic calcium transient amplitudes summated supralinearity (Figure 4c–h), with effect sizes closely resembling those observed in the drug-free condition (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 7 dendrites shown in Figure 4c-h.

claim: The effect sizes of supralinear summation in TTX closely resembled those observed in the drug-free condition in neurogliaform cells.
source: Across all dendrites tested (n=7), both the uEPSP and the dendritic calcium transient amplitudes summated supralinearity (Figure 4c–h), with effect sizes closely resembling those observed in the drug-free condition (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental data in Figure 4 and Figure 2.

claim: Voltage-gated sodium channels do not contribute to supralinear dendritic integration in NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons.
source: The data argue against a contribution of voltage-gated sodium channels to supralinear dendritic integration in NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the TTX experiments showing persistent supralinearity.

claim: A subset of neurogliaform cells continued to show supralinear summation for both peak and integral in the presence of nimodipine.
source: In another group of neurogliaform cells, we examined dendritic integration in the presence of the L-type voltage-dependent calcium channel blocker nimodipine. Although the population average non-linearity was not different from 0, a subset of neurons continued to show supralinear summation for both peak and integral (Figure 5a and c–f), contrasting with the effect of blocking NMDARs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a and c-f.

claim: Dendritic calcium transients in neurogliaform cells were profoundly attenuated by nimodipine.
source: Dendritic calcium transients were profoundly attenuated (Figure 5b, g and h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b, g and h.

claim: L-type calcium channels have a smaller contribution to voltage supralinearity than NMDARs in neurogliaform cells.
source: We tentatively conclude that L-type calcium channels have a smaller contribution to voltage supralinearity than NMDARs, but contribute substantially to dendritic calcium influx.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the nimodipine experiments.

claim: L-type calcium channels contribute substantially to dendritic calcium influx in neurogliaform cells.
source: We tentatively conclude that L-type calcium channels have a smaller contribution to voltage supralinearity than NMDARs, but contribute substantially to dendritic calcium influx.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the nimodipine experiments showing reduced calcium transients.

claim: Voltage supralinearity persisted in neurogliaform cells in the presence of CPA.
source: We next asked if release from intracellular stores also contributes to dendritic calcium transients, as has been reported in stratum oriens interneurons (Camiré and Topolnik, 2014). We therefore examined the effect of depleting calcium stores with the SERCA inhibitor cyclopiazonic acid (CPA). Although voltage supralinearity persisted (Figure 6a and c–f), dendritic calcium transients were abolished (Figure 6b, g and h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a and c-f.

claim: Dendritic calcium transients in neurogliaform cells were abolished by CPA.
source: We next asked if release from intracellular stores also contributes to dendritic calcium transients, as has been reported in stratum oriens interneurons (Camiré and Topolnik, 2014). We therefore examined the effect of depleting calcium stores with the SERCA inhibitor cyclopiazonic acid (CPA). Although voltage supralinearity persisted (Figure 6a and c–f), dendritic calcium transients were abolished (Figure 6b, g and h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b, g and h.

claim: NMDARs are the main driver of regenerative currents in the dendrites of neurogliaform cells.
source: A parsimonious explanation for the dissociation of voltage supralinearity and calcium signalling is that NMDARs are the main driver of regenerative currents in the dendrites of neurogliaform cells, and that calcium influx via NMDARs and L-type calcium channels is amplified by calcium release from intracellular stores.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined pharmacological experiments.

claim: Calcium influx via NMDARs and L-type calcium channels is amplified by calcium release from intracellular stores in neurogliaform cells.
source: A parsimonious explanation for the dissociation of voltage supralinearity and calcium signalling is that NMDARs are the main driver of regenerative currents in the dendrites of neurogliaform cells, and that calcium influx via NMDARs and L-type calcium channels is amplified by calcium release from intracellular stores.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined pharmacological experiments.

claim: The robust NMDAR-mediated supralinearity demonstrated in neurogliaform cells stands in contrast to the more subtle supralinearity observed in PV+ interneurons in response to an identical glutamate uncaging protocol.
source: Overall, the robust NMDAR-mediated supralinearity demonstrated in neurogliaform cells stands in contrast to the more subtle supralinearity observed in PV+ interneurons in response to an identical glutamate uncaging protocol, which was confined to dendrites in stratum oriens (Cornford et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim compares the current findings to prior research.

claim: Uncaging-evoked uEPSPs summated supralinearly in OLM cells.
source: Uncaging-evoked uEPSPs summated supralinearly in OLM cells, as detected by comparing either the peak amplitude or voltage integral of near-synchronously evoked responses to the arithmetic sum of the asynchronously evoked responses (Figure 7c–g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c-g.

claim: NMDAR blockade abolished supralinearity in OLM cells.
source: As for neurogliaform cells, there was no obvious dependence of the magnitude of supralinearity on the average size of the individual uEPSPs, dendritic distance, dendrite order, or dendrite diameter (Figure 7—figure supplement 1). NMDAR blockade abolished supralinearity (Figure 8a–e), further underlining the similarity with neurogliaform cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a-e.

claim: Sublinear summation was not observed in D-AP5 in OLM cells.
source: However, sublinear summation was not observed in D-AP5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with D-AP5 in OLM cells.

claim: The uEPSPs evoked in OLM cells (with NMDARs intact) were sub-threshold for detectable dendritic calcium signals under the recording conditions.
source: Another striking difference was that the uEPSPs evoked in OLM cells (with NMDARs intact) were sub-threshold for detectable dendritic calcium signals under our recording conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the absence of detectable calcium signals in OLM cells.

claim: Neither sodium channel blockade nor calcium channel blockade prevented supralinear summation of uEPSPs in OLM interneurons.
source: Neither sodium channel blockade (Figure 8f–j), nor calcium channel blockade (Figure 8k–o) prevented supralinear summation of uEPSPs in OLM interneurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8f-j and 8k-o.

claim: Depletion of intracellular calcium stores with CPA had no effect on supralinear summation in OLM interneurons.
source: Depletion of intracellular calcium stores with CPA also had no effect (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Supralinearity in OLM cells is mediated exclusively by NMDARs.
source: The data thus point to a model where supralinearity is mediated exclusively by NMDARs, and occurs with uEPSPs that are subthreshold for dendritic calcium signalling.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the pharmacological experiments in OLM cells.

claim: Supralinearity in OLM cells occurs with uEPSPs that are subthreshold for dendritic calcium signalling.
source: The data thus point to a model where supralinearity is mediated exclusively by NMDARs, and occurs with uEPSPs that are subthreshold for dendritic calcium signalling.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the absence of calcium signals in OLM cells.

claim: The supralinearity for voltage integral in OLM interneurons was significantly smaller than that in neurogliaform cells.
source: When neurogliaform and OLM data obtained in TTX were grouped together with the data without blockers, the supralinearity for voltage integral in OLM interneurons was significantly smaller than that in neurogliaform cells (Figure 8p).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 8p.

claim: The local dendrite diameter of neurogliaform interneurons was significantly lower than that of OLM cells.
source: Consistent with such a pattern, the local dendrite diameter of neurogliaform interneurons was significantly lower than that of OLM cells (Figure 8q).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological measurements shown in Figure 8q.

claim: Both hippocampal neurogliaform interneurons and OLM cells exhibit robust NMDAR-dependent supralinear integration of dendritic uEPSPs recorded at the soma.
source: The main results of the present study are that both hippocampal neurogliaform interneurons and OLM cells exhibit robust NMDAR-dependent supralinear integration of dendritic uEPSPs recorded at the soma.
evidence: This claim summarizes the main experimental findings.

claim: Supralinear NMDAR-dependent integration was observed by measuring dendritic calcium fluorescence transients in neurogliaform cells.
source: Supralinear NMDAR-dependent integration was also observed by measuring dendritic calcium fluorescence transients in neurogliaform cells, which were sensitive to blockade of L-type calcium channels or depletion of intracellular stores.
evidence: This claim summarizes the calcium imaging findings in neurogliaform cells.

claim: Near-synchronous glutamate uncaging that was sufficient to elicit NMDAR-dependent boosting of uEPSPs failed to recruit detectable dendritic calcium transients in OLM cells.
source: However, near-synchronous glutamate uncaging that was sufficient to elicit NMDAR-dependent boosting of uEPSPs failed to recruit detectable dendritic calcium transients in OLM cells.
evidence: This claim summarizes the difference between neurogliaform and OLM cells.

claim: No role for voltage-gated sodium channels in dendritic integration of uEPSPs was observed in either neurogliaform or OLM cells.
source: In contrast to principal neurons, we observed no role for voltage-gated sodium channels in dendritic integration of uEPSPs in either cell type.
evidence: This claim summarizes the TTX experiments in both cell types.

claim: Clustered synaptic receptor activation leads to relief of voltage-dependent block of dendritic NMDARs by magnesium ions, accounting for supralinear summation of uEPSPs recorded at the soma.
source: Taken together, the data are consistent with a model where clustered synaptic receptor activation leads to relief of voltage-dependent block of dendritic NMDARs by magnesium ions, accounting for supralinear summation of uEPSPs recorded at the soma.
evidence: This claim is a mechanistic interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: In neurogliaform cells, L-type voltage-gated calcium channels are recruited by local depolarization.
source: In neurogliaform cells (although apparently not in OLM cells) L-type voltage-gated calcium channels are also recruited by the local depolarization, and together with calcium influx via NMDARs, the resulting local elevation of intracellular calcium triggers further release from intracellular stores, thereby amplifying the dendritic calcium concentration transient.
evidence: This claim is a mechanistic interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: In neurogliaform cells, calcium influx via NMDARs and L-type calcium channels triggers release from intracellular stores, thereby amplifying the dendritic calcium concentration transient.
source: In neurogliaform cells (although apparently not in OLM cells) L-type voltage-gated calcium channels are also recruited by the local depolarization, and together with calcium influx via NMDARs, the resulting local elevation of intracellular calcium triggers further release from intracellular stores, thereby amplifying the dendritic calcium concentration transient.
evidence: This claim is a mechanistic interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The dependence of supralinear dendritic summation on NMDARs but not voltage-gated sodium channels is reminiscent to the pattern observed at dendrites of parvalbumin-positive interneurons in stratum oriens.
source: The dependence of supralinear dendritic summation on NMDARs but not voltage-gated sodium channels is reminiscent to the pattern observed at dendrites of parvalbumin-positive interneurons in stratum oriens (Cornford et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim compares the current findings to prior research.

claim: NMDARs contribute to long-term potentiation in neurogliaform cells.
source: NMDARs have previously been implicated in synaptic signalling in neurogliaform cells (Chittajallu et al., 2017; Price et al., 2005; Armstrong et al., 2011) and also contribute to long-term potentiation (Mercier et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The ratio of NMDAR- to AMPAR-mediated signalling at glutamatergic synapses on neurogliaform cells is higher than in other hippocampal interneuron subtypes.
source: Indeed, the ratio of NMDAR- to AMPAR-mediated signalling at glutamatergic synapses on neurogliaform cells has been shown to be higher than in other hippocampal interneuron subtypes (Chittajallu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The high ratio of NMDAR- to AMPAR-mediated signalling may explain why NMDAR-mediated supralinear integration is especially prominent in neurogliaform cells.
source: This feature may explain why NMDAR-mediated supralinear integration is especially prominent in neurogliaform cells, although a further contribution may come from their unusually thin and short dendrites, which would be expected to represent a high impedance, thus facilitating their depolarization by glutamate receptor activation.
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The unusually thin and short dendrites of neurogliaform cells would be expected to represent a high impedance, thus facilitating their depolarization by glutamate receptor activation.
source: This feature may explain why NMDAR-mediated supralinear integration is especially prominent in neurogliaform cells, although a further contribution may come from their unusually thin and short dendrites, which would be expected to represent a high impedance, thus facilitating their depolarization by glutamate receptor activation.
evidence: This claim is based on biophysical principles and morphological observations.

claim: OLM cells exhibited smaller supralinear voltage integration compared to neurogliaform cells.
source: OLM cells exhibited several differences in comparison with neurogliaform cells. First, supralinear voltage integration was smaller.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing the two cell types.

claim: Blockade of NMDARs led to linear, as opposed to sublinear summation of uEPSPs in OLM cells.
source: Second, blockade of NMDARs led to linear, as opposed to sublinear summation of uEPSPs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with D-AP5 in OLM cells.

claim: The differences between OLM and neurogliaform cells can be explained by a relatively lower expression of NMDARs and/or lower dendritic impedance in OLM cells.
source: These differences can be explained by a relatively lower expression of NMDARs and/or lower dendritic impedance as expected from larger dendritic diameter and length.
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The dendrites of OLM cells are equipped with sparse thin spines.
source: A further morphological difference is that the dendrites of OLM cells are equipped with sparse thin spines (Martina et al., 2000; Maccaferri et al., 2000), although we did not visualize them.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The density of both spines and NMDA receptors differ with distance from the soma in the dendrites of OLM cells.
source: The density of both spines and NMDA receptors have also been reported to differ with distance from the soma in the dendrites of OLM cells (Gramuntell et al., 2021; Guirado et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: OLM cells have been reported to boost dendritic signals via active sodium conductances when increasing amounts of current were injected into the dendrites.
source: Whilst we saw no evidence suggesting sodium-channel-dependent supralinear voltage integration in OLM cells, OLM cells have been reported to boost dendritic signals via active sodium conductances when increasing amounts of current were injected into the dendrites (Martina et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The uncaging stimulation protocol remained subthreshold for the initiation of sodium-channel-dependent boosting in OLM cells.
source: This difference may be due to the uncaging stimulation protocol remaining subthreshold for the initiation of sodium-channel-dependent boosting, as current injection seemed to remain linear until EPSPs became greater than ~20 mV in amplitude (Martina et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation comparing the current findings to prior research.

claim: The present study highlights the ability of both neurogliaform and OLM neurons to perform local computations upstream of the site of axonal action potential initiation.
source: The present study highlights the ability of both neurogliaform and OLM neurons to perform local computations upstream of the site of axonal action potential initiation.
evidence: This claim is an interpretation of the overall findings.

claim: Synaptic inputs converging to common dendritic domains in principal neurons have been shown to exhibit correlated activity.
source: In principal neurons, synaptic inputs converging to common dendritic domains have been shown to exhibit correlated activity (Iacaruso et al., 2017; Takahashi et al., 2012; Wilson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Synaptically evoked calcium transients in dendritic domains of interneurons of the visual cortex exhibit orientation tuning that is not apparent in the global activity recorded at the soma.
source: Synaptically evoked calcium transients in dendritic domains of interneurons of the visual cortex have also been reported to exhibit orientation tuning that is not apparent in the global activity recorded at the soma (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The dendritic nonlinearities uncovered by the present study, together with different forms of synaptic plasticity described in interneurons, are a candidate mechanism to achieve organization of information processing.
source: The dendritic nonlinearities uncovered by the present study, together with different forms of synaptic plasticity described in interneurons (Kullmann et al., 2012), are a candidate mechanism to achieve such an organization of information processing.
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation of the findings.
